The research results show that the proposed model based on the DSC has good noise resistance and stability for each control loop, demonstrated based on Lyapunov criteria. The quality of the controller is verified by numerical simulation using Matlab-Simulink. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and practical application of the proposed model and trajectory tracking control algorithm.

articleTitle: Quality of Service-based Multi-Task Scheduling for Cooperative Multi-radar Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, an algorithm based on quality of service (QoS) framework is proposed to address the multitask scheduling problem in complex collaborative multi-radar scenarios. The task scheduling problem is described as an NP-hard mixed integer optimization problem in terms of task quality and task efficiency. To efficiently tackle the characteristic of the optimization problem, we proposed a two-step decoupling algorithm based on convex relaxation focusing on optimizing overall performance. Then, two comparison algorithms are proposed in this paper to benchmark against the proposed task scheduling algorithm. By contrasting these algorithms with the proposed approach, the study assesses the effectiveness and superiority of the new method in optimizing task utility and addressing the challenges of multi-task scheduling in multi-radar cooperative surveillance scenarios.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors Using Simultaneous Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The quadrotor has found extensive applications across a spectrum of fields, including environmental research, military operations, transportation, and firefighting. The design of its control system can be approached using various methodologies such as sliding mode control, backstepping, and model predictive control (MPC). The primary objective of the control system is to achieve trajectory tracking while simultaneously avoiding collisions with obstacles. In this paper, a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) strategy is adopted for calculating control inputs that guide the quadrotor along a desired trajectory while ensuring obstacle avoidance. The obstacle avoidance constraints that are formulated pose a nonlinear and intricate challenge, rendering the optimization problem complex for the nonlinear program solver to address. To tackle this, linear constraints representing hyperplanes between the quadrotor and obstacles are employed. These hyperplanes dynamically adjust as the quadrotor moves, thereby averting collisions effectively. The application of NMPC to quadrotor control, as demonstrated in this paper, underscores the suitability and practicality of the proposed approach. It successfully showcases the efficacy of NMPC in facilitating quadrotor control while navigating through complex environments.

articleTitle: Keynote Speaker #2 : Exploring and exploiting the universality phenomenon in high-dimensional estimation and learning
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Universality is a fascinating high-dimensional phenomenon that points to the existence of universal laws. These laws govern the macroscopic behavior of a wide array of large and complex systems, despite their microscopic differences. The notion of universality originated in statistical mechanics, particularly in the study of phase transitions. Similar phenomena have been observed in various fields such as probability theory, dynamical systems, random matrix theory, and number theory.

articleTitle: Verification of State Based Slow HTTP DDoS Prevention Method
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: S1ow HTTP DDoS attacks involve sending numerous requests to a web server at a low rate, prolonging connection durations to saturate the server’s connection pool and disrupt legitimate client access. Detection based on traffic volume monitoring is challenging because of the low traffic volume generated per unit time. Furthermore, attackers employ tactics, such as controlling request transmission rates, timing, and connection durations, to make detection more difficult. Existing mitigation methods statistically process the packet characteristics of an attack, taking at least approximately 20 s for identification and mitigation. Additionally, the false-positive rate for legitimate connections has not been considered, necessitating validation in real-world environments. We proposed a fast detection method that observes the state transitions for each flow of HTTP communication on the network path, cutting off incomplete connections that exceed predefined thresholds for connection duration and idle time. Using data captured from actual attacks, we conducted detection experiments, achieving an average detection and mitigation time of 10 s from the start of the attack. The identification accuracy, as measured by the F1 Score, was 0.986, and the false-positive rate was 0.0096. However, there are concerns about accidentally disconnecting legitimate traffic when applying this method to web servers handling a large number of HTTP communications. Therefore, in this study, we used a web server simulating real-world operations to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and measured a false positive rate of 0.0013, confirming the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Socially Aware Robot Navigation Framework: Automatic Detecting and Autonomously Approaching People in Unknown Dynamic Social Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this study, we propose a socially aware navigation framework that enables a mobile robot to automatically detect humans and navigate autonomously and safely to approach the detected humans. To do that the proposed framework make uses of a real-time appearance-based mapping (RTAB-Map) technique, which is RGB-D SLAM approach. The RTAB-Map method is based on the global loop closure detector with real-time constraints to generate 3D point clouds of the surrounding environment and create a 2D occupancy grid map for navigation process. The proposed framework also applies a frontier-based exploration approach, consisting of a flexible framework to decide a proper goal for mapping and exploring. Finally, the YOLO model is adopted to detect the human during the exploration process of the mobile robot. The simulation result illustrates that the mobile robot equipped with the proposed framework is able to automatically detect the human and navigate autonomously and safely to the detected humans in unknown dynamic environments

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication AGVs for Industrial Product Transportation with High Load Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This article presents the results of designing and fabrication an automatic guided vehicle (AGV) with the ability to carry a large load of up to 300kg. It is designed to serve a number of heavy cargo transport tasks with two independent conveyors placed directly above. The model is named G2J with a length of 1800mm and a width of 1200mm. Its mechanical structure is basically analyzed for stress and deformation based on information about loads and material properties of the system. G2J is designed with four drive wheels and is controlled by magnetic line tracking with a line detection sensor system, magnetic card reader and warning system. G2J can receive remote control commands via PLC processor and wireless communication. The system can be stored for 30 different movement scenarios in the production area. Lidar sensors identify objects in the scanning area and collision sensors help G2J receive early warnings and increase its safety level during movement. The information display block meets the ability to monitor and evaluate the operating status of the entire system when performing functions. The first version of the G2J system has been manufactured in practice and initially meets the design requirements. Some issues of precise control and evaluation of system motion according to programmed orbits will continue to be completed in the near future.

articleTitle: Dimensional Lifting, Finite-Time Convergence, and Bearing-Only Algorithms for the Fermat-Weber Location Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, some novel results on the Fermat Weber Location Problem (FWLP) with stationary beacons are reported. We propose using dimensional lifting to prevent collision between the agent and the beacons and bearing-only control laws to guide an agent to the Fermat-Weber point. To improving convergence rate, finite-time bearing-only control laws are also provided. The stability and robustness of the Fermat-Weber point under the proposed algorithms are asserted from a control approach and supported by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Fast Terminal Sliding-Mode Control with High-Gain Observer for Series Elastic Actuator Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Series Elastic Actuator (SEA) robots play an important role in applications that require precise force control, interaction with humans, adaptability, and reliable performance. However, because SEA incorporates a compliant element, such as a spring or an elastic material, precise position control is difficult to obtain. To solve this problem, in this paper, fast terminal sliding mode control is applied to design position control for the SEA robot. In addition, a High Gain Observer (HGO) is also developed to observe the system state variables instead of measuring them. The efficiency of the proposed control algorithm is demonstrated through simulation. A comparison of the fast terminal sliding mode to conventional sliding mode control has been done. The results show that the fast terminal sliding mode control shows a better performance in terms of control input and position accuracy with the SEA robot system.

articleTitle: Maneuvering Target Tracking with Turn-Rate Learning Using Dirichlet Processes
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Accurately tracking maneuvering targets is a challenging task due to the inherent difficulty in precisely modeling their dynamics in advance. To achieve good tracking performance, it is crucial for an estimator that the predicted dynamics closely matches the actual motion during maneuvers. Typically, constant turn models with preset turn-rates are incorporated into the interacting multiple model (IMM) estimator to address maneuvering target tracking. However, the finite number of models in the model set, determined by prior knowledge, fails to cover all possible maneuvers, which leads to tracking performance degradation when unexpected maneuvers occur. To overcome this limitation, we propose a turn-rate learning scheme for maneuvering target tracking based on Dirichlet processes (DP). By employing DP to model the evolution behavior of the turn-rate, our algorithm exhibits the ability to learn various turn-rates and adapt the model set more effectively. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the superior tracking accuracy of our proposed algorithm compared with the IMM algorithm.

articleTitle: Improving Gaussian Sum Filter to Implement In-motion Yaw Alignment for Quadrotor Attitude Control
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper presents a new type of integration between the Global Positioning System and Inertial Measurement Unit (GPS/IMU) to provide a higher in-motion yaw alignment accuracy under large initial heading errors when magnetometer data are not reliable. In order to quickly determine the yaw angle without relying on assumptions about the dynamics of the quadrotor, velocities measured from GPS are fused with accelerations and angular velocities measured from the IMU. In contrast to the conventional Gaussian sum filter (GSF), in this paper the forecast weights of the Gaussian mixture model are updated in the time update step of basic estimators, including complementary filters (CF) and extended Kalman filters (EKF). This reduces the number of Gaussian models used in the GSF and speeds up computation on embedded system hardware.

articleTitle: Application of through surface perforation for aircraft flow parameters control
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The paper considers the aerodynamic characteristics of solid and perforated plates of different configurations at the incoming flow velocity $V_{\infty}$ = 25m/s and angles of attack 0° $\leq \alpha \leq$ 90°, describes the effect of perforation on the flow structure near the plate surface, and analyzes the influence of the degree of perforation and internal cavity on the aerodynamic characteristics and flow structures. The aerodynamic coefficients of the considered plates were calculated by numerical simulation in the FlowVision software package, smoke visualization was used to obtain experimental flow structures. Based on the results of the work, conclusions are drawn about the efficiency of using aircraft controls having the form of flat perforated plates.

articleTitle: GP-Based Track Segment Association in Limited Field of View
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In practice, target tracking often suffers from track breakage due to sensor limitation and the target’s agile movements. To enhance track continuity, track segment association technology is commonly employed. However, existing approaches heavily rely on dynamic model, which require significant prior knowledge that can be difficult to obtain in practical scenarios. In contrast, this study proposes a novel track segment association method based on Gaussian Process (GP). As a data-driven approach, GP can learn from the data, reducing the dependence on prior knowledge. Simulation results demonstrate that employing GP for track segment association leads to improved accuracy and correctness compared with model-based methods.

articleTitle: Object-Oriented Semantic Mapping for Reliable UAVs Navigation
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: To autonomously navigate in real-world environments, special in search and rescue operations, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) necessitate comprehensive maps to ensure safety. However, the prevalent metric map often lacks semantic information crucial for holistic scene comprehension. In this paper, we proposed a system to construct a probabilistic metric map enriched with object information extracted from the environment from RGB-D images. Our approach combines a state-of-the-art YOLOv8-based object detection framework at the front end and a 2D SLAM method - CartoGrapher at the back end. To effectively track and position semantic object classes extracted from the front-end interface, we employ the innovative BoT-SORT methodology. A novel association method is introduced to extract the position of objects and then project it with the metric map. Unlike previous research, our approach takes into reliable navigating in the environment with various hollow bottom objects. The output of our system is a probabilistic map, which significantly enhances the map’s representation by incorporating object-specific attributes, encompassing class distinctions, accurate positioning, and object heights. A number of experiments have been conducted to evaluate our proposed approach. The results show that the robot can effectively produce augmented semantic maps containing several objects (notably chairs and desks). Furthermore, our system is evaluated within an embedded computer - Jetson Xavier AGX unit to demonstrate the use case in real-world applications.

articleTitle: FEM simulation of SAW H2 gas sensor based on Pd/AlN/Si multilayer structure
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The SAW (Surface Acoustic Wave) sensor for measuring H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas is a type of sensor based on the phenomenon of changing surface acoustic wave velocity. In this study, we propose a Finite Element Method (FEM) simulation model of multilayer structure for SAW to measure H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas based on a two-port delay line sensor. AlN/Si substrate was chosen due to its high surface velocity thus potentially increasing sensitivity. In addition, Pd was selected to combine with AlN/Si because of its high absorption of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The FEM simulation results show that the center frequency decreases from 127.41 MHz to 127.36 MHz, while the hydrogen ratio in palladium increases from 0.0 to 0.3. In the process of changing the temperature from $27^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $107^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, the center frequency of the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> SAW sensor decreases from 128.67 MHz to 128.54 MHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Force Measurement Apparatus for Electrical Coil Investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Typically, an electromagnet can be used as an electrical actuator to provide contactless forces, it is crucial to identify and govern the characteristics that impact the attraction force between the electromagnet and the target object in order to ensure precision in contactless force control. This research undertakes the development of an electromagnetic force measurement apparatus (EFMA) to investigate the factors affecting electromagnets actively. The paper assesses the influence of both distance and current on the electromagnet attraction force. Several experimental tests were put in place to determine the accuracy of the model and successfully draw conclusions about the relationship between parameters.

articleTitle: The modelling of the doubly fed induction machine as a wind power generator with consideration of the chaotic phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The doubly-fed induction generator system (DFIG) has certain advantages, so it has been widely applied in practice. However, the DFIG is a dynamic system with strong nonlinearity and a complex structure, so the system is likely to encounter problems during operation. Any error under certain conditions can cause the system to fall into a chaotic working state, causing the system’s working quality to deteriorate and even cause the system to be destroyed if not done properly and promptly remedied. This study proposes to model the DFIG system taking into account the chaotic state in a comprehensive form, and at the same time build an online Lyapunov exponent calculation module, to promptly detect the chaotic working state of the system during the operating process, thereby taking corrective measures early (control to eliminate the risk of chaos) to avoid widespread errors that cause serious consequences for the system.

articleTitle: Design and Manufacturing of Axle Counting Equipment
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The axle counting equipment is one of the important devices in the railway signal control system, which helps the system to operate safely and accurately. Currently, the axle counting devices commonly used in the Vietnamese railway signaling system are mainly imported. This article presents a solution for manufacturing axle counting equipment for Vietnamese railways. The operation principle of the axle counting sensor is based on the change of the magnetic flux through the receiving coil when the wheel passes the sensors. The signal processing of the alxe counter based on the amplitude and phase of the voltage received from the receiver coil will recognize the state of the wheel occupying the sensor space. Sensors and processing circuits have been successfully fabricated and tested on several routes in Vietnam railways. The results show that the signal threshold between passing train and no train is clearly distinctive. The count value of axle is transmitted to the Control center through a highly reliable CAN communication network. The manufactured devices can be applied to Automatic Warning System at level crossings, Automatic Block Signaling, Centralized Traffic Control.

articleTitle: Evaluation Of Flux-barriers For Synchronous Reluctance Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper introduces two distinct methods for enhancing the electromagnetic torque and output power of synchronous reluctance motors (SynRMs). These approaches are developed by taking into account two specific motor models: SynRM 1 with equal geometry flux barriers and SynRM 2 with optimized geometry flux barriers. In the SynRM 1, all the flux-barriers have the same bridge thickness, outer thickness, inner thickness; The number of flux-barriers is considered. In the SynRM 2, the optimal number of flux-barriers is selected from the SynRM 1. By changing the geometry of the flux-barriers, the motor’s design is enhanced to minimize torque ripple, leading to smoother operation and improved performance. Next, a finite element technique is applied to calculate and simulate electromagnetic parameters, such as the flux density, average torque and output power. As a result of the analytical modeling, the SynRM is designed with 4 flux-barriers and different geometries of flux-barrier to improve the torque ripple and torque characteristic of SynRM motor.

articleTitle: PyBoFormer: Pyramid Selected Boundary Transformer for Polyp Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Polyp segmentation has become increasingly important in recent years, prompting the development of various techniques such as CNN, and Transformer-based methods to obtain excellent results. However, these methods frequently encounter challenges in the loss of crucial local details such as boundaries and small objects, which play a vital role in the segmentation task. To address this issue, we introduce a new state-of-the-art model for polyp segmentation, the PyBoFormer, which uses a Transformer encoder Mvit and a stage-wise feature pyramid decoder structure to improve the generalization ability of models. Specifically, Global-Local Context Aggregation (GLCA) module gains the ability to aggregate and represent both global and local features, facilitating precise localization of large and small objects. The results obtained by our method demonstrate its superiority over other approaches, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of Dice, IoU metrics on various polyp databases including Kvasir-SEG, CVC-300, Eltis, and ClinicDB.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Fault-tolerant controller for wheeled mobile robots with faulty actuators
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This article introduces a fault-tolerant control scheme for a two-wheeled mobile robot. The focus of this model is to address the impact of faults within the actuators, a critical aspect that significantly impacts the robot’s performance and operational efficiency. An observer is designed to monitor the dynamic state of the robot’s system, allowing it to promptly identify and assess the actuator’s faults that may arise during its operation. Based on this data, the extent of the fault’s influence on the overall system is estimated, providing essential information for subsequent control decisions. Analyzing and synthesizing control laws are built on mathematics and Lyapunov stability theory. The simulation is done by MATLAB-Simulink to validate the efficiency of the proposed control law, contributing valuable insights to the domain of robotics and control engineering.

articleTitle: Model Reference Adaptive Tracking Control for 2-DOF Active Magnetic Bearing Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This work investigates the problem of tracking control for 2-degree-of-freedom active magnetic bearings modeled as nonlinear systems with input noise. We propose an adaptive tracking control algorithm for the active magnetic bearing system. Input to state stable stabilization is developed to track errors smoothly and converges to an arbitrarily sufficient small area around the neighborhood of the origin. Thanks to Lyapunov’s theory, the stability of the closed-loop system is demonstrated. Finally, a simulation result of the tracking problem of the active magnetic bearing system is introduced to illustrate the efficiency of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Refined Tracking Filtering Algorithm Based on IMM
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Maneuvering targets, distinguished by their pronounced dynamic characteristics, present significant challenges to radar tracking. To address these problems, a refined tracking method based on IMM (IMM-RTF) is proposed in this paper. The key idea of the method is to adaptively correct the recursive residual covariance by using the observation residual based on the consistency of residual and residual covariance to reduce the influence of model mismatch. In addition, to realize refined filtering, this paper analyzes the influence of model mismatch on the filter, and models the consistency problem of residual and residual covariance as a convex optimization problem. By analyzing the unique structure of the problem, the analytical solution of the problem under two assumptions is derived. Meanwhile, the adaptive IMM framework is adopted, thus effectively improving the tracking performance of maneuvering targets and non-maneuvering targets under steady-state conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that compared with the IMM, the IMM-RTF not only accentuates the tracking precision for maneuvering targets in steady states but also significantly fortifies target tracking robustness amidst model mismatch.

articleTitle: Bearing-Based Network Localization Under Randomized Gossip Protocol
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a randomized gossip algorithm for the bearing-based network localization problem. Let each sensor node be able to obtain the bearing vectors and communicate its position estimates with several neighboring agents. Each update involves two agents, and the update sequence follows a stochastic process. Under the assumption that the network is infinitesimally bearing rigid and contains at least two beacon nodes, we show that when the updating step-size is properly selected, the proposed algorithm can successfully estimate the actual sensor nodes’ positions with probability one. The randomized update provides a simple, distributed, and cost-effective method for localizing the network. The theoretical result is supported with a simulation of a 1089-node sensor network.

articleTitle: Plug-and-Play Feature for Automotive Camera Sensors Using ReCoIN Model With Smart Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Plug-and-Play (PnP) from an automotive industry context means enabling the sensors from the Automotive Perception System (APS) to be effortlessly incorporated into the vehicle’s architecture without requiring too many intricate changes. The goal behind this is to set up simple configurations, easy replacement of components, and establish compatibility with varied vehicle models. However, the vital problem with PnP is the lack of standardized interfaces that makes development, testing, and validation of software features more challenging. While AUTOSAR (AUTomotive Open System ARchitecture) and other standards have made significant advancements in the same field, there still exist challenges that have to be addressed, such as flexible configurations and compatibility. These are due to tight coupling between sensor hardware and its associated software applications. Hence, the motivation behind decoupling these components is the idea of having the opportunity to PnP from any sensor supplier with minimal impact on software applications and reduced verification and validation.The automotive sensors are manufactured and developed based on specific requirements from the Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) by various sensor suppliers. OEMs have a dependency built up when the hardware components are supplied by the sensor suppliers based on certain requirements. In this case, the OEMs design and develop the software applications focusing on the underlying sensor hardware capabilities, which is an imprecise approach to PnP.This paper introduces a concept in pursuance of uniformity of data called “ReCoIN” with a smart configuration method to tackle the problems that are faced to achieve both abstraction and PnP of automotive camera sensors. It also provides experimental outcomes with the help of different Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Ballbot systems: A benchmark with Hierarchical Sliding Mode and Linear Quadratic controls
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This study presents the Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) method for ballbot systems. Due to the complex nature of the underactuated system, ballbot requires a controller capable of ensuring both goals: moving to the desired position and maintaining the balance of the body throughout the moving process. NMPC is an optimal control method based on a predictive model to calculate the states of the ballbot after a certain period of time in the future. Moreover, NMPC can optimize the position, tilt angle and control signal through the cost function and handle special constraints of the system. Simulation results show that NMPC is more effective than some previous techniques such as LQR and HSMC in terms of safety constraints of tilt angle and input-output signals.

articleTitle: Information Gain-weighted Multi-sensor Arithmetic Average Fusion Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel multi-sensor Kalman filter (KF) based on the arithmetic average (AA) fusion method. In this approach, the fusing weights are designed according to the online Kalman gain matrix obtained from each local filter. Both the standard KF and the unscented KF (UKF) are applied to linear and nonlinear state space models, respectively. Simulation results demonstrate the superior target tracking performance of our approach compared to the recently proposed suboptimal AA fusion method using the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD) in both linear and nonlinear scenarios.

articleTitle: Distributed Posterior Fusion for Vehicle Tracking with Gaussian Processes
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: We focus on the distributed posterior fusion for vehicle tracking in this paper. With rectangular prior information of vehicles’ shapes, we build a non-zero mean Gaussian Processes (GP) model to initialize the extents. In order to improve the estimation accuracy of targets’ kinematic and extent states, we try to make progress in two aspects. For one thing, we propose the unscented Kalman extended target Probability Hypothesis Density (UK-ET-PHD) filter with a tailor-made GP model. It can track multiple targets simultaneously and solve the nonlinear problems. For another thing, we realize the posterior fusion using the Generalized Covariance Intersection (GCI) rule with the proposed UK-ET-PHD local trackers. Finally, we evaluate the performance of the proposed method in the view of both vehicles’ position and extent estimation.

articleTitle: Dense-U-Net assisted Localization of Speech Sources in Motion under Reverberant conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning (DL) approach, based on dense convolutional neural networks, to improve the localization of target sources in motion using the steered response power-phase transform (SRP-PHAT) concept. The SRPPHAT method is a state-of-the-art acoustic source localization (ASL) technique and can be regarded as a filter-and-sum (F-S) beam-former, which is based on the summation of generalized cross-correlation (GCC) components and constructs an acoustic power map (APM) depicting the position estimates of the target sources. However, under strong reverberation and noise, the GCC components are adversely affected leading to inaccuracies in the computation of the SRP-PHAT. Recent advances in DL have shown the capability of DL algorithms to outperform traditional methods of ASL, under noisy, reverberant conditions. However, most of these methods are dependent on microphone array geometry and other environmental conditions available during the training phase. Alternative DL methods such as encoder-decoder structures have been recently applied to denoise the generalized cross-correlation-phase transform (GCC-PHAT) components before constructing the SRP-PHAT, which have demonstrated good performance under reverberant conditions. While conventional encoder-decoder structures can be helpful, incorporation of a dense block within an encoder-decoder framework arranged in a U-Net structure can lead to better performance under severe reverberation and background noise. In this work, we propose the application of a U-Net with dense block (Dense-U-Net) to de-noise the GCC-PHAT components which can lead to the construction of a refined APM. Computer simulations demonstrate that this process yields an improved localization of target sources in motion under reverberant, noisy conditions in an indoor environment.

articleTitle: Wearable device to support stroke patient during lower limb rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: IoMT (Internet of Medical Things) is the combination of data from health measuring devices and mobile applications with a health management system, enabling remote disease treatment by healthcare professionals. This research aimed to design an IoMT system that can evaluate the rehabilitation of stroke patients through active range of motion exercises and send the data to physiologists to remotely assess the patient’s recovery. The system was developed using gyroscope sensors to calculate the range of motion (ROM) when patients perform rehabilitation exercises by sitting in a chair and extending their legs in front of them. It also utilizes microcontrollers for the purpose of displaying the completed repetitions on an LCD screen and transmitting data to the supervisor through the Blynk application. The initial test results were quite promising, as the system accurately tallied the number of completed repetitions, displayed it on the LCD screen, and alerted patients with a buzzer upon each exercise completion. Additionally, it measured and stored data regarding various angles of motion, which were then displayed in real-time on both the application and the LCD screen. (The number of degrees may be adjusted by the physiotherapist based on each patient’s condition.

articleTitle: Decode-and-Forward Based Cooperative MIMO System using Deep Learning for Wireless Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this article, we introduce a Decode-and-Forward (DF) based cooperative Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system using autoencoder (AE) technique, abbreviated as AE-DF, for Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN). In our scheme, the source, relay, and destination nodes are designed using neural networks, forming an AE. The learning parameters of the AE are trained synchronously through two sequential phases, allowing for optimal synchronization of the entire system. Additionally, in order to effectively reduce co-channel interference (CCI) in the received signal streams and enhance the bit error rate (BER) performance of the AE-DF system, we introduce the Minimum Mean Square Error Network (MMSEnet) detector employing deep learning at the relay and destination node. We assess the performance of these systems in scenarios with perfect channel state information (CSI) and imperfect CSI. The simulation results demonstrate that our system significantly outperforms the baseline system which is the conventional DF-based cooperative MIMO system using Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) detector.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for Tracked Mobile Robot Under Slip Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Tracked mobile robots have played an essential role in transportation, especially in off-road conditions. The behavior of tracked mobile robots in outdoor off-road conditions is quite different from those working in structured indoor environments. It requires consideration of many challenging issues such as slip and sinkage phenomena. The slipping parameters, which generate a large accumulating positioning error in vehicles, are usually unknown and change suddenly during operating through different terrains or moving from linear lines to curved lines. Therefore, these unknown parameters should be estimated, and the control system of the tracked mobile robot still achieves good tracking performance and robustness, irrespective of how abruptly the slipping parameters vary. This paper proposes the slip parameter adaptive sliding mode controller as the low-level controller for the tracked mobile robot to track a desired trajectory. The adaptive control scheme allows the tracked mobile robot to be controlled accurately without the knowledge of slipping parameters. A simulation is conducted to validate the efficiency of the proposed controller.

articleTitle: Coherent Integration and Detection for Extended Targets in Traffic Scenes
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper intends to address the problem of detecting high speed and maneuvering extended target in wideband radars with the idea of coherent integration (CI). Due to the extended target energy spillover may occur in adjacent range bins, along with the shadowing effect of contiguous scattering centers (SCs), the robust detection of weak extended target is a challenging problem. Both of the range migration (RM) effect and Doppler frequency migration (DFM) will be introduced in target returns due to high maneuverability. To address these problems, two CI methods called modified Keystone transform (MKT) and modified Radon Fourier transform (MRFT) are proposed for high speed and maneuvering extended target detection. To mitigate the disturbance caused by DFM, the phase compensation with two-order motion parameter is constructed to prevent energy dispersion in the Doppler frequency domain. Then, the Keystone transform (KT) and Radon Fourier transform (RFT) are applied for range walk correction, respectively. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is validated by numerical simulations of four typical traffic scenes.

articleTitle: Adaptive Dynamic Programming and Decentralized Optimal Output Regulation of Two-Time-Scale Interconnected Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, we address the decentralized optimal output regulation problem for two-time-scale (TTS) interconnected systems with unknown slow dynamics through adaptive dynamic programming (ADP). Firstly, singular perturbation theory is leveraged to decompose the TTS interconnected system into a slow subsystem and several interconnected fast time-scale subsystems. Secondly, we develop a decentralized optimal control scheme for the fast time-scale subsystems with interconnections. Also, we devise an off-policy ADP algorithm to learn the optimal control strategy for the slow time-scale subsystem with unknown dynamics. Moreover, we combine the slow and fast control strategies to design the composite decentralized optimal output regulator. Both optimality and stability of the closed-loop system are rigorously analyzed. Finally, simulation results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: The Smooth Trajectory Estimator for LMB Filters
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper proposes a smooth-trajectory estimator for the labelled multi-Bernoulli (LMB) filter by exploiting the special structure of the generalised labelled multi-Bernoulli (GLMB) filter. We devise a simple and intuitive approach to store the best association map when approximating the GLMB random finite set (RFS) to the LMB RFS. In particular, we construct a smooth-trajectory estimator (i.e., an estimator over the entire trajectories of labelled estimates) for the LMB filter based on the history of the best association map and all of the measurements up to the current time. Experimental results under two challenging scenarios demonstrate significant tracking accuracy improvements with negligible additional computational time compared to the conventional LMB filter.

articleTitle: A Multiple Marker Design for Precision and Redundant Visual Landing in Drone Delivery
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Drone delivery has been one of the promising applications of drones in real life. Precision Landing is an important mission to deliver the package to the customer’s place. Visual marker has been studied to provide accuracy in pose estimation during landing based on a downward camera since GPS localization may be disrupted at low altitude due to high building occlusions. However, there are still some remaining issues of previous visual marker design such as the trade-off between detection altitude and marker size, lack of redundancies, weakness to motion blur, occlusions on the landing pad and possible issues related to the utilization of a single marker family. This paper proposed a multiple marker design for precision and redundant visual landing combining multiple types of marker families: Whycon, Aruco and AprilTag. The design and respective algorithms to detect multiple markers on the design have been evaluated in both photo-realistic simulation and practical environments. A smooth and precise trajectory for visual landing is successfully performed from the altitude of 25 m even in the case of occlusions or possible issues happened with one of the marker detector algorithms.

articleTitle: EMG-based Assessment Device for Hand Rehabilitation with Cloud Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Stroke has become a prevalent cardiovascular ailment that impacts human lives due to aging, chronic health issues, or injuries. Often, stroke survivors require rehabilitation to regain muscle function and relearn their motor skills. Unfortunately, the insufficient availability of rehabilitation services and a shortage of practitioners impede their recovery progress. Therefore, the development of an assessment device for hand rehabilitation based on electromyography (EMG) is proposed. The main challenge is to design an assessment device that can recognize the user’s motion intention, which can be done by utilizing the electromyogram signals generated by forearm muscles contributed by the movement and/or grasping abilities of the hand. In this research, an EMG-mechanical sensor fusion is designed which combines an electronic conditioning circuit that measures the EMG signals extracted from the forearm muscles with mechanical sensor modalities (self-assembled hand dynamometer and flex sensor for wrist angle measurement). Once the proof of concept is established, the designed system is interfaced with the data analytics platform. This platform stores the collected data in the cloud, making it accessible for rehabilitation assessment. Scikit-Fuzzy with multiple linear regression is used to model the relationship between EMG signals, handgrip force, and wrist angle and map it to the hand assessment score chart. Based on the analysis, the trained model using Fuzzy with multiple linear regression achieved a 73.32% prediction accuracy. The proposed research contributes towards the aim of providing better rehabilitation diagnostic for post-stroke hand impairment survivors in regaining their hand strength and functionality and improving their quality of life.

articleTitle: Synthesis of the Optimal Algorithm to Detect the Maneuvering Direction of the Supermaneuverable Separating Target
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The paper demonstrates a method to synthesize an optimal algorithm for detecting the maneuvering direction of a supermaneuverable target separated from a group, which is an air-to-air missile launched from the target group. The purpose of the algorithm is to decide whether the missile separated from the target group being tracked is “towards the intercepting missiles” or “not towards the intercepting missiles.” Based on that decision, the control system on board the interceptor missile will automatically decide if the tracking mode has to be switched. If the separating missile is heading “towards the intercepting missiles,” the interceptor will remain the original tracking mode because the enemy missile finds itself. On the contrary, if the direction of the separating missile is “not towards the intercepting missiles”, it is considered a high-risk target that needs to be destroyed. Consequently, the interceptor must track the separating missile to protect other objects of the interceptor group.

Author Keywords: Algorithm to detect the maneuvering direction of separating missiles

articleTitle: Theoretical Model for Dynamic Analysis of Soft Eel Robot’s Underwater Motions Based on Mechanics of Multibody System
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Soft robotics has posed unique challenges in dynamic analysis and motion control, particularly in contrast to conventional rigid robots. This paper introduces a theoretical approach for evaluating the dynamic behavior of an underwater soft eel robot - our previous soft robot design. Based on the concept of a pseudo-rigid-body model, we propose an equivalent dynamic model for the eel robot, converting its flexible body into an assembly of traditional rigid links and joints. Subsequently, utilizing the mechanics of multibody system dynamics, we derive explicit dynamic equations governing the underwater locomotion of the eel robot. The configuration parameters and external forces of the dynamic model are determined. Then the dynamic equations are solved with different scenarios to explore the effect of pneumatic pressure frequency and amplitude on the robot’s dynamic response. The theoretical calculations are compared with preliminary experimental results, demonstrating the robustness and reliability of the proposed dynamic model. This dynamic model is expected to become a valuable approach for the analysis and control of soft eel robots and diverse soft robotic systems.

articleTitle: Deep Clustering Based Latent Representation for IoT Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The Internet of Things with a billion connected devices can generate a huge amount of data daily. This poses challenges to security tasks (i.e. identifying IoT malware). Our previous studies used analytic techniques to reduce the data size and extract valuable information. Currently, clustering is a key technique for many data-driven applications, and it has been widely studied with different distance functions and algorithms. One research direction is to use representation learning for clustering. This research proposes a combination of Deep Clustering AutoEncoder (DCAE) with anomaly detection algorithms for an end-to-end anomaly detection framework. The DCAE maps the data from the original space to a lower-dimensional latent space, where it iteratively minimizes the clustering loss. Then, the output of DCAE is fed to algorithms such as Isolation Forest (IF), $K -$nearest Neighbors (KNN), Local Outlier Factor (LOF), and One-class Support Vector Machine (OCSVM) for identifying anomalies. The proposed model is evaluated on nine recent devices in the N-BaIoT dataset and measure their performance. The experimental results show that the new latent representation improves the IoT outlier detection methods significantly. The model’s time efficiency is also recorded to assess its suitability for practical applications.

articleTitle: Collision checking trajectories-based motion planning systems for autonomous mobile robots in dynamic human environments
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In order to enhance the safety and efficiency of autonomous mobile robot navigation within dynamic environments, it becomes crucial for the robot to proactively anticipate potential collisions with humans. This study introduces a innovative Trajectory Elastic Band model, termed the Collision Prediction Time Elastic Band model (CPTEB), designed for online trajectory planning. The central concept behind this model revolves around the detection of possible collision trajectories between the robot and predicted human trajectories within the robot’s proximity, achieved by checking collision points. To evaluate the model’s efficacy, a series of experiments was conducted within simulated environments. The simulation results decisively highlight the robot’s proactive avoidance of humans in its vicinity, thereby ensuring the safe and effective accomplishment of its objectives.

articleTitle: A Decision Support System for off-gas and steam optimal management in integrated steelworks
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Optimizing the energy distribution in energy intensive industries is a difficult task. It requires a global vision for synchronizing the energy demands of all the involved processes. In this work, a decision support system is presented, which aims at supporting process operators and plant managers in monitoring and control of energy flows, e.g., process off-gases, steam and electricity in integrated steelworks. The software includes a digital twin of the integrated steelworks, for modelling or predicting internal energy production and consumption, exploited by a hierarchical control system that calculates in real-time the scheduling of the power plant, steam boilers and all the involved manipulable equipment. The digital twin implements a wide set of continuous learning models based on machine learning methodologies and standard system identification techniques. The control system integrates a high-level controller for calculating optimal references for a time horizon up to one day. These references are exploited by a set of distributed economic model predictive controllers that focus on optimizing the behavior of each specific energy network. This system allows minimizing the waste of energy, and minimizing the costs’ management, by improving the synchronization of the main energy actors.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Unifying Object Re-Identification and Cross-view Geo-localization on Autonomous UAVs
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of Unmanned Autonomous Vehicles (UAVs) technologies, the applications of autonomous UAVs in aerial surveillance-related missions have been increasing. These missions often involve image processing-related tasks, such as object (human, vehicle) detection, re-identification, image-based localization, and navigation. However, these tasks often require much computation to achieve the best performance, which is quite a challenge for autonomous UAVs due to the limitation of hardware and computing resources on these devices. Unfortunately, no architecture has been established to perform these tasks adequately. In this study, for the first time, we combine three tasks that can significantly contribute to the operation of autonomous UAVs in real-life missions: Person Re-Identification, Vehicle Re-Identification, and Cross-view Geo-Localization. We exploit the generalization ability of currently available deep metric learning methods and propose a framework to learn to re-identify objects (humans, vehicles) and perform geo-localization simultaneously. The proposed method was evaluated on benchmark UAV datasets and received promising results.

articleTitle: Transformer based Online Continuous Multi-Target Tracking with State Regression
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Multi-target Tracking (MTT) is the process of processing received measurements to maintain estimates of the current status of multiple targets, with important applications to autonomous driving, aerial reconnaissance, underwater operations, and others. In the model-based setting, Bayesian filtering can provide the theoretical optimal estimate in a single target scenario. However, in complex situations, uncertain factors such as changes in the number of targets will cause the amount of calculation to increase exponentially, resulting in a decline in tracking accuracy. To solve that problem, model-free methods based on deep-learning provide an attractive alternative, especially the state-of-the-art architecture Transformer based encoder-decoder prediction model, which outperforms the Bayesian filters in the single frame prediction tasks. However, when switching to continuous tracking, these algorithms need to be trained separately frame by frame to adapt to the new tasks. Still, there is no correlation between their predictions from different frames, which prevents them from fully utilizing all the measurements. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end Transformer based MTT method with state autoregression, which allows the model to have the capability of online continuous tracking and make total use of the entire trajectory. The results show that the proposed model is a great extension from single-frame prediction to online continuous tracking.

articleTitle: Energy and Time-Efficient Scheduling of Automated Guided Vehicles System: A Hybrid Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm and Improved Ant Colony Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid implementation of the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithm and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) is applied for optimal scheduling and path-planning for an automated guided vehicle system (AGVS), in terms of energy consumption and service tardiness. AGVS is an essential component in the modern flexible manufacturing complex for transporting materials and goods. High efficiency in the operation of the AGVS contributes to an increase in the stability of the whole manufacturing process, improving total production efficiency and profit. ABC and ACO algorithms are swarm intelligence methods based on the foraging behavior of honeybees and ants colonies in real-life. The proposed strategy is the combination of the local search ability of ACO and global search ability of ABC to avoid the local optimum trap of solutions. The approach demonstrates satisfactory performance based on different case studies in simulation for a large-scale AGV system, in comparison with other optimization methods. Results show that while the proposed method may not be the best in terms of the total travel distance, it allows for the safe travel of the AGV while still outperforming the original solutions in terms of time and energy cost.

articleTitle: Transformer Architecture Based Multi-frame TBD Algorithms for Maneuvering Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The multi-frame track-before-detect (MF-TBD) algorithm can effectively improve the tracking performance of the target in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scenarios by considering all reasonable paths. However, when the target undergoes maneuvering motion, there will be a mismatch between the actual model and the assumed model. It leads to a sharp decline in algorithm performance. In this paper, a model-free trajectory sequence prediction network based on transformer architecture is studied for maneuvering targets. The network is trained using trajectory sequences from multiple types of target models to estimate the state of the target in different maneuvering characteristics. The trajectory sequence prediction network is integrated into MFTBD, replacing the target model, and the specific process of the improved MF-TBD algorithm is provided. The simulation results demonstrate the superior performance and flexible adaptability of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Adaptive finite time extended state observer for varying rope length tower cranes
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper proposes a new control algorithm, the second-order sliding mode control (SO-SMC) based on adaptive finite time extended state observer (AFT-ESO) for a threedimensional tower crane (3DTC) system. The 3DTC system is an un-actuated and nonlinear system, the motion of the load depends on the movement of the trolley, the turntable, and the length of the rope. Furthermore, the 3DTC system working in an outdoor environment is heavily influenced by external disturbance, affecting the control performance and the ability to measure the system states. Therefore, an adaptive finite time extended state observer is proposed to solve these problems. The AFT-ESO estimates the state variables and the total disturbance (including the external disturbances and the uncertainty component) accurately, which creates the premise to build a second-order sliding mode control based on AFT-ESO that ensures a globally stable closed-loop system and controls the load to follow the reference trajectory to the desired position. Finally, simulation results are provided to confirm the effectiveness and sustainability of the proposed algorithm.

Author Keywords: Adaptive finite time extended state observer

articleTitle: Development of electric drive system for solar battery system based on artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this article, the authors present research on the influence of the drive system that controls the solar battery system according to sunlight, to maximize the source of incoming solar radiation PV panels. This drive system tracking operates according to the changing solar radiation light entering the PV panel; When the sun changes its position and shines on the solar battery system, the motor will rotate, causing the panel to move according to the sun’s light. The system is researched to build a model and calculate the position tracking control algorithm, according to [12, 15] and combined with reinforcement learning technology with Q-learning algorithm and MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracker) control). These studies will bring maximum capacity to the grid-connected solar power system. These research results will be the basis for establishing control algorithms and designing solar power systems in industry and military.

articleTitle: ZSL-SLCNN: Zero-Shot Learning with Semantic Label CNN for Malware Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Malware is becoming increasingly sophisticated, with new malware constantly emerging, posing challenges for cybersecurity teams to classify them accurately. Traditional supervised learning methods have achieved impressive results recently, thanks to the contributions of various novel techniques and models. However, a notable drawback of this approach is its inability to classify malicious code it has never encountered, in other words, with untrained labels. Zero-shot Learning has been explored in diverse fields to address this limitation, but its performance still needs to improve. Notably, most current studies only focus on one-layer mapping, with few outstanding achievements, and studies using zero-shot learning in malware classification need to be improved. In this paper, we propose a novel method utilizing Semantic Labels with two-layer mapping to enhance the efficiency of traditional Zero-Shot Learning. This study explores how zero-shot learning can be leveraged to detect image-based malware using merely simple CNN and pre-trained word embedding as semantic labels. Through experimental results, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method for classifying both seen and unseen malware families.

articleTitle: An Information-Theoretic Approach to Complementary Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper presents the challenges of divergence-based sensor fusion methods in multi-target tracking applications where sensors have different fields of view. We propose an alternative approach to GCI fusion that is particularly devised for the fusion of labeled multi-Bernoulli densities. In our approach, we present the observation that fusion could be separately performed for each object label over the single-Bernoulli densities associated with that label, and the fusion weights could then be tuned according to the detectability of the object by each sensor. The resulting solution is tested in a challenging numerical experiment where up to 10 vehicles are moving and tracked by various dynamic and static sensors. The results show the advantages of our proposed method when compared to GCI fusion and the complementary fusion methods.

articleTitle: Rotating Machinery Bearing Fault Diagnosis via Transfer Learning Based on Subdomain Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Rotating machinery (RM) is utilized extensively in various industrial applications, primarily due to its dependable operation is essential for optimizing productivity and preventing costly downtime. Accurate and early bearing fault diagnosis in RM is crucial to prevent machinery breakdown and maintain optimal performance. In this study, we propose a novel method for rotating machinery bearing fault diagnosis based on transfer learning with subdomain adaptation. Our method leverages the knowledge acquired from a source domain that contains labeled data for both healthy and faulty conditions. By transferring this knowledge to a target domain with labeled data limitation, our approach addresses the scarcity of labeled data in the target domain. We specifically focus on adapting the domain shift by computing the discrepancy between the source and target domains through subdomain adaptation. To validate the effectiveness of our proposed approach, extensive experiments were carried out on a large-scale CWRU dataset that encompasses various bearing operation conditions. The experimental outcomes reveal that our transfer learning-based fault diagnosis method achieves 93.8% to 100.0% in diagnostic accuracy and outperforms conventional methods.

articleTitle: Temporal Multiple Rotation Averaging: A Multi-Camera Dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive time-series image dataset tailored to evaluate multi-target tracking within a dynamic sensor network using multiple rotation averaging techniques. Recognizing the significant gap in the availability of datasets—particularly those offering details on camera orientations and positions—our dataset stands out by comprising images from multiple vehicles equipped with cameras navigating through a common environment. Each image in the series is supplemented with exact ground truth values for the respective camera’s orientation and location at every discrete time step. Such a rich dataset is a vital resource for techniques aiming to deduce camera positions and orientations and finds relevance in target tracking and information fusion tasks. Going beyond mere introduction, we leverage this dataset to showcase the superiority of our newly proposed temporal multiple-rotating averaging method. When juxtaposed with prevailing non-temporal techniques, our method manifests a markedly enhanced accuracy, underlining its potential for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Predicting Respiration Rate using Acceleration Sensors and LSTM: A novel Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The significance of appraising respiratory rate as a determinant of sleep quality has achieved a firm foundation within the literature. This has led to the emergence of numerous technological solutions encompassing both non-contact and wearable modalities, leveraging sensor mechanisms encompassing cameras, radar, wireless communication, and accelerometers, with the objective of estimating respiratory frequencies. Nevertheless, the efficacy of non-contact methodologies has frequently been compromised when confronted with constrained environmental circumstances, exemplified by low illumination levels and tangible obstructions. Conversely, ongoing investigative endeavors targeting wearable apparatuses have exhibited a predilection for machine learning paradigms; however, the potential for more advanced and precise deep learning models remains inadequately harnessed. Identifying the potential for enhancement, this work presented a novel approach for estimating respiration rates. This involves a synergistic fusion of an accelerometer and an LSTM deep learning model, resulting in superior predictive capabilities for respiratory rate compared to their individual performances. In this experiment, data were collected from 10 teenagers with dynamic respiration rates during various sleep postures (lateral left, lateral right, supine, prone, and sitting). The experiment achieved ±1.962 MAE error in estimating respiratory rates.

articleTitle: Enhancing Thyroid Cancer Detection Through Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Thyroid cancer poses a significant challenge in terms of accurate diagnosis due to its complexity and diverse clinical manifestations. Recent advancements in machine - learning techniques have demonstrated their potential to enhance the accuracy of cancer detection. In this study, we aimed to develop a machine-learning model for the detection of thyroid cancer utilizing a comprehensive dataset of various clinical variables. Multiple machine - learning algorithms were trained and evaluated to predict the presence of cancer. Our findings revealed a significant achievement, with the developed methodology achieving an accuracy of approximately 82%. This represents a notable improvement over existing diagnostic methods and underscores the potential of machine - learning in assisting clinicians in making more accurate and efficient thyroid cancer diagnoses. Further refinements and prospective studies are necessary to validate the generalizability and clinical utility of our model. Nevertheless, our study highlights the substantial promise of machine - learning algorithms in enhancing thyroid cancer detection and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Deep Reinforcement Learning with Priority-based Socially Aware Mobile Robot Navigation Frameworks
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Socially aware robot navigation is a multi-objective decision-making problem. Nonetheless, the attempt to address this issue using single-objective reinforcement learning raises substantial challenges when it comes to extending navigation policies to accommodate the intricate demands of human social interactions. Our work presents a versatile framework for expanding existing robot navigation capabilities into the realm of multi-objective decision-making. This framework empowers users to easily specify their preferences without the burden of extensive engineering efforts. Experimental findings clearly demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in guiding an existing reinforcement learning system toward the optimization of navigation policies in alignment with user-defined preferences.

articleTitle: Power Optimization and ARSs Selection in Uplink Cell-Free Multi-ARSs Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Cell-Free (CF) is one of the techniques that play a crucial role in the evolution of current 5th Generation (5G) technology to satisfy the needs of emerging communication applications. In this paper, we analyze the uplink CF system utilizing multiple aerial relay stations (ARSs), where ARSs are defined as unmanned aerial vehicles functioning as relay stations. ARSs are designed with multiple antennas that concurrently serve a specific number of terrestrial users in a given area. In terms of signal processing, the system uses the time division duplex (TDD) protocol for communication and the minimum mean squared error (MMSE) method for channel estimation. We determine the uplink user throughput expression by applying the matched filtering (MF) technique and optimize pilot/data transmission power to enhance system quality using the successive convex approximation (SCA) method and the linear problem (LP), respectively. Additionally, we propose an ARS selection strategy based on the large-scale fading factor to reduce system load, computational complexity, and energy consumption for ARSs. The results indicate that addressing the power optimization problem improves user throughput. Furthermore, the findings also reveal that when a certain number of ARSs are selected, the ARS selection method outperforms the CF (no selection) technique in terms of the user throughput. Accordingly, we discover the best number of ARSs for the proposed system.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms for Parkinson’s Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease is a progressive condition that impacts the neurological system and the areas of the body that are under the control of the nerves. Detecting and diagnosing PD early and accurately is essential for effective treatment and care. Biomedical speech analysis has emerged as a promising noninvasive approach for detecting and monitoring PD. We collected a data set from the University of California at Irvine (UCI) machine learning repository. The study investigates the utilization of a dataset to assess the suitability of machine learning (ML) algorithms for diagnosing Parkinson’s disease. The research employs classification algorithms coupled with feature selection based on Pearson correlation. The data set is comprised of 195 voice recordings obtained from 31 patients during their examinations. Among them, 23 individuals in the study were diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. The age at the time of diagnosis ranged from 46 to 85 years. To handle this data, three methodologies are employed: a train/test split, k-fold cross-validation, and stratified k-fold cross-validation to ensure robust evaluation. Additionally, we use the F1 score, accuracy, and balanced accuracy measures to evaluate our models. The highly correlated selection data combined with data processing methods helps achieve positive results for all machine learning algorithms. Especially, Random Forest consistently outperformed other methods in our project. Random Forest with an accuracy of 95.42%, balanced accuracy of 93.98%, and an f1-score of 0.98. This demonstrates the capability of algorithms to diagnose Parkinson’s disease effectively, even when confronted with imbalanced data. In our future research, we aim to integrate additional data on Parkinson’s Disease in order to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of this condition.

articleTitle: Uncovering the Resilience of Binarized Spiking Neural Networks under Adversarial Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The Binarized Spiking Neural Network (BSNN)-a Spiking Neural Network with binary weights, is particularly suitable for Edge-AI hardware architectures thanks to its simplicity in data format and computing functions. However, like other SNNs, BSNNs could be directly trained or converted from Artificial Neural Networks using the gradient principle. They hence are highly susceptible to adversarial attacks. This study focuses on investigating the resilience of BSNNs against adversarial attacks. We assess the robustness of BSNNs through FGSM and PGD attacks on the Fashion-MNIST dataset. This work marks the first implementation of adversarial attack and defense tailored to the BSNNs. Our results show that adversarial training significantly enhances the robustness of BSNNs against adversarial attacks compared to the original model. Improving the resilience of BSNN opens doors to its potential applications in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Power Allocation for Multiple Sensing and Communication Tasks Using Massive MIMO Base Station
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a joint sensing and communication scenario with the simultaneous implementation of multiple sensing and communication tasks employing a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) base station system. This system operates on orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) modulations for both communication and sensing signals. To evaluate the performance of dual functions, we derive the lower bound on the achievable downlink rate for communication and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) for radar detection. By focusing on the power allocation strategy, we propose two optimization cases with different emphasis on sensing and communication to explore the trade-off between radar performance and communication quality. The formulated optimization problem can be effectively solved via the binary search technique, and simulation results demonstrate its efficiency.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sliding Mode-based Observer and Current Controller for Torque Balance Control Strategy of Coaxial BLDC Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In underwater vehicle applications, coaxial brushless direct current (BLDC) motors, serving as thrust actuators, present significant challenges. These challenges encompass external disturbances induced by environmental factors and internal perturbations arising from rapid temperature and electrical parameter fluctuations. To address these issues, this study introduces an Adaptive Sliding Mode Control (ASMC) algorithm, employing field-oriented control techniques, and incorporates a Sliding Mode Observer (SMO) to mitigate the aforementioned disturbances. Additionally, a three-level inverter structure, accompanied by a Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) algorithm tailored for high-power applications to minimize harmonic distortion, has been implemented. Subsequently, a torque balance control strategy is developed, based on the master-slave speed tracking method, incorporating all these control structures and algorithms. The reliability and effectiveness of the proposed controller are substantiated through comprehensive simulation analyses conducted using Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Label Space Partition Selection for Multi-Object Tracking Using Two-Layer Partitioning
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Estimating the trajectories of multi-objects poses a significant challenge due to data association ambiguity, which leads to a substantial increase in computational requirements. To address such problems, a divide-and-conquer manner has been employed with parallel computation. In this strategy, distinguished objects that have unique labels are grouped based on their statistical dependencies, the intersection of predicted measurements. Several geometry approaches have been used for label grouping since finding all intersected label pairs is clearly infeasible for large-scale tracking problems. This paper proposes an efficient implementation of label grouping for label- partitioned generalized labeled multi-Bernoulli filter framework using a secondary partitioning technique. This allows for parallel computation in the label graph indexing step, avoiding generating and eliminating duplicate comparisons. Additionally, we compare the performance of the proposed technique with several efficient spatial searching algorithms.
