The results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed approach on large-scale data sets, enabling scalable trajectory estimation.

articleTitle: 3D-INSEG: A 3D Instance Segmentation Algorithm for Extended Object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Classical multiple object tracking (MOT) algorithms were based on the assumption of single targets yielding single measurements. Recently there has been significant work which relaxes this assumption by addressing extended target tracking in which it is assumed that a single target can yield multiple measurements. To provide these multiple measurements, robust detections are a central challenge in Multiple Extended Object Tracking (MEOT). In this article, we propose the 3D INStance SEGmentation (3D-INSEG) algorithm to address this problem by harnessing the capabilities of stereo cameras and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for both depth estimation and segmentation in 3D space. By utilizing stereo vision, we obtain depth information, which complements the 2D segmentation produced by a CNN-based model. The segmentation results are projected into the 3D space using the depth information. To validate the effectiveness of the approach, we conduct comparisons with traditional clustering techniques, specifically with Velodyne LIght Detection And Ranging (LIDAR) data points. Depth values are estimated from the RAFT-stereo algorithm, and the Mask-RCNN model performs 2D segmentation in the image plane. The robustness of the approach is currently demonstrated based on single human tracking and its potential extension to general MEOT is discussed.

articleTitle: A Motion Status Discrimination Method Based on Velocity Estimation Embedded in Multi-object Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Multi-object tracking(MOT) has been a research hotspot in the field of computer vision. Currently, the most popular tracking paradigm involves first using object detection models to process the images, and then combining methods such as Kalman filtering for tracking. This paradigm has achieved good results on various datasets, but it lacks the ability to accurately determine whether an object is in motion. In certain scenarios, researchers may be interested only in moving objects and desire information specifically related to their motion, without the need for information about stationary objects. However, there has been limited research on determining the motion state of targets in the field of multi-object tracking. To address this issue, this paper proposes a velocity-based motion state discrimination method for object tracking. This method can be integrated with different multi-object tracking methods to provide more information about the tracking results. Additionally, we evaluate the effectiveness of the method on a custom dataset and test it on selected scenes of the re-annotated CDnet-2014 dataset. The experimental results demonstrate significant achievements of our proposed method. When combined with the YOLOv8+StrongSORT tracking method, the motion state discrimination accuracy (F1 score) of our method reaches 0.6975 on the custom dataset and 0.7831 on the CDnet-2014, showcasing the practicality of our method.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Hierarchical Combination of CG-TAS and ED-TAS to Improve BER Performance at Low Complexity for VASM Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The spatial modulation (SM) technique has been extended with various variants, one of which is variable active antenna spatial modulation (VASM), where the count of activated transmit antennas varies according to the input bit sequence. This approach offers significant enhancements to the spectral efficiency and flexibility of VASM in comparison to conventional SM systems. Channel gain (CG) and Euclidean distance (ED) are widely adopted criteria for transmit antenna selection (TAS) in SM systems. CG-TAS provides low computational complexity; however, it exhibits a slight improvement in bit error rate (BER) performance. Conversely, ED-TAS optimally enhances BER performance at the cost of higher computational complexity. This paper proposes a novel low-complexity TAS method, named HC-TAS, that hierarchically combines CG-TAS with ED-TAS for the VASM systems. A comprehensive analysis of computational complexity demonstrates HC-TAS’s superiority over ED-TAS in alleviating the workload burden. Furthermore, Monte Carlo simulation results indicate that HC-TAS outperforms CG-TAS and approximates ED-TAS in enhancing BER performance.

articleTitle: Integration of Intelligent Driver Model with Interaction-Aware LMB (IA-LMB) Filter for Vehicle tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Vehicle tracking is one of the most common applications of multi-object tracking. In the context of Bayesian filtering, including accurate information about the tracking scenario tends to improve tracking performance. However, in some cases, including more information increases the complexity of the tracking system. This paper presents a novel method of direct mathematical incorporation of accurate motion models for vehicles, specifically the intelligent driver model (IDM), within the interaction-aware labeled multi-Bernoulli (IA-LMB) filter. The proposed method provides the inclusion of a more accurate vehicle motion model into the IA-LMB filter without increasing the complexity of the IA-LMB filter. The proposed filter outperforms traditional methods, which do not consider interactions between targets such as the PHD filter and the LMB filter. Moreover, the proposed method outperforms the original IA-LMB filter for the interacting vehicles owing to more accurate modeling of vehicle motion, and hence the inclusion of interactions. The performance of the proposed method has been evaluated using the optimal sub-pattern assignment (OSPA) metric for the overall simulation and the mean square error (MSE) for the interacting vehicles.

articleTitle: An Iterative Steered Response Power Algorithm for Multi-Source Localization and Counting Using Distributed Microphone Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: The well-known steered response power-phase transform (SRP-PHAT) algorithm has been demonstrated to be robust under adverse acoustic conditions for single-source localization. When applying this algorithm to the localization of multiple concurrent sound sources, one may encounter a problem that some sources dominate over the others over short time intervals, resulting in fewer significant SRP peaks being found than the true number of sources. This problem makes it difficult to detect all the sources among the available SRP peaks. This paper proposes an iterative SRP approach to jointly estimating the number of sources and their locations in a distributed microphone network. The proposed approach is derived based on the time-frequency (T-F) bins selected by a combination of two weighting schemes, one using the coherence, and the other using signal-to-noise ratio. At each iteration, a dominant source is localized by exploiting the highest SRP peak and its contribution is removed by eliminating the T-F bins that are dominated by this source. When iteration stops, a set of coarse location estimates are obtained, which are further refined by merging the closely located sources based on their distances. Experimental results demonstrate the robustness of the proposed algorithm to reverberation and noise.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization of Deep Auto-Encoder Network Architectures for Anomaly-based Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Deep Auto-Encoder (DAE) is a neural network model that is commonly used to develop anomaly-based network intrusion detection systems. However, the architecture of existing models are all arbitrary designs with no theoretical basis or empirical formula. As a result, it will cost computational and storage resources as well as not being able to learn the best data representation space. In this paper, we propose a novel method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) for searching the optimal architecture of DAE for anomaly-based network intrusion detection systems, named PSODAE. Our proposed model can find the optimal number of neurons on the hidden layers of DAE. Therefore, the meaningful, prominent, concise latent representation space can be learned from network data, which better supports the performance of network anomaly detectors. We conduct experiments using standard datasets including NSLKDD, UNSW-NB15, CICIDS-2017, and five scenarios in dataset CTU13. The experimental results have generated the optimal architecture of DAE models on each dataset. This study proposes an effective way of designing deep learning network architecture to develop modern network intrusion detection systems.

articleTitle: A Fast GP Regression Method Using Banded Sparsification of Inverse Covariance
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Modeling and prediction using Gaussian processes (GPs) have widespread applications in machine learning, information processing, automatic control, biology, and other fields. However, GP regression requires a computational complexity of $O(N^{3})$. To overcome this issue, this paper proposes a fast GP regression method based on a banded sparsification of the inverse covariance matrix. It follows that we first propose an approximate inversion algorithm rooted in the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, which exhibits approximately linear computational complexity. Furthermore, we demonstrate it is essentially a higher-order Gaussian Markov process (GMP) model and minimum mean square error (MMSE) estimation. Next, by transforming the inverse covariance matrix into a banded sparse structure, we derive a more efficient GP regression algorithm, of which the core is to employ a high-order GMP model to effectively approximate the general GP.

articleTitle: IoT based Labware Tracking during Mobile Robot Transportation
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: Mobile robots are increasingly being used to automate life science laboratories. Intelligent, easy-to-implement methods must be developed for tracking labware and samples. Modern solutions based on IoT (Internet of Things) methods are ideal here. This paper presents a novel approach for localizing IoT labware during mobile robot transportation in the laboratory using Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) beacons. A comprehensive data collection system, including BLE beacons, an IoT module, an IoT cloud, and a visual interface is provided. The BLE beacon features are extensively evaluated under various settings to ensure accurate and reliable tracking. By strategically deploying BLE beacons throughout the laboratory and placing the IoT module on the transportation tray, real-time monitoring of laboratory equipment during mobile robot movement is possible. This practical solution enhances laboratory efficiency and seamlessly integrates IoT functionalities, facilitating efficient management of lab equipment in the life science laboratory.

articleTitle: Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for Control and Command of Multi-UAV Communication with Finite Blocklength
publicationTitle: 2023 12th International Conference on Control, Automation and Information Sciences (ICCAIS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze a system where a single ground control station (GCS) is applied to control and command multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). To again the fading and interference, the rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) scheme and the multi-input multi-output (MIMO) strategy are used. Moreover, since the message in control and command is small, the finite blocklength is also considered in this system. To evaluate system performance, we derive blocklength error rate (BLER) where UAVs and GCS are equipped with multiple antennas operating in Nakagami-m fading channels. Our approach employs Gaussian-Chebyshev quadrature approximation and first-order Riemann integration to formulate BLER expressions. The BLER values offer insights to determine optimal common stream, UAV altitudes, and power allocation for common signals. Furthermore, we investigate the substantial influence of deployment environments and line-of-sight (LoS) probability on the system performance. Numerical results are used to validate the accuracy of our analysis.
